LegacyBase.prereq: V-M-010 (SecurityCtx sandbox for .before path resolution), V-M-011 (editorWithTabs mode switching contract), V-M-012 (muya state preservation across mode transitions), V-M-002 (fs commands for .before file reading), V-M-003 (watcher integration for live diff refresh on external changes)
LegacyBase.module-surface: Renderer: src/renderer/src/components/editorWithTabs/diffView.vue — new Vue SFC wrapping CodeMirror 5 MergeView addon. Pattern follows existing src/renderer/src/components/editorWithTabs/sourceCode.vue (shared editor chrome, lifecycle hooks, theme wiring). MergeView instantiated with `origLeft` (baseline) and `value` (current content), using diff-match-patch as the diff algorithm provider. Supports inline (combined pane, default) and side-by-side (two-pane, toggle via toolbar button) modes with synchronized scrolling. Renderer: src/renderer/src/components/editorWithTabs/index.vue — extended with third editor mode 'diff' alongside 'wysiwyg' and 'sourceCode'. Cmd+D keyboard shortcut toggles diff mode on/off. When entering diff mode, current content captured and baseline fetched via Tauri invoke `mt_diff_baseline`. When exiting, previous mode (wysiwyg or sourceCode) restored. diffView component conditionally mounted via v-if alongside existing editor components. Renderer: src/renderer/src/store/editor.js — per-tab state extended with `diffMode: boolean`, `diffBaseline: string|null`, `diffBaselineSource: 'file'|'git'|null` fields. Tab state persisted across tab switches. Backend: src-tauri/src/m031_diff.rs — new Tauri command `mt_diff_baseline` accepting file path, returning `{ baseline: String, source: "file"|"git" }`. Resolution order: (1) check for `{path}.before` sibling file, (2) if in git repo, attempt `git show HEAD:{relative_path}`, (3) return error with reason. All paths validated through SecurityCtx sandbox. Git invocation uses `std::process::Command` with timeout. Backend: src-tauri/src/main.rs — register `mt_diff_baseline` in Builder invoke_handler chain. Dependencies: `diff-match-patch` npm package (new, ~8KB gzip); `codemirror/addon/merge/merge.js` (already installed, ~38KB); `codemirror/addon/merge/merge.css` (already installed). Auto-detect: when a file is opened and a `.before` sibling exists, diff mode is automatically suggested/activated (configurable via preference `autoDiffOnBeforeFile`, default true).

high-level-scenarios.S1: inline-diff-additions — open file with .before baseline containing 3 new paragraphs added; MergeView renders green-highlighted additions inline with gutter markers; BLOCK_DIFF_RENDERED mode=inline lines_added=N.
high-level-scenarios.S2: inline-diff-deletions — baseline contains paragraphs removed in current file; MergeView renders red-highlighted deletions inline with strikethrough; deleted line count matches expected.
high-level-scenarios.S3: inline-diff-modifications — mixed additions and deletions (paragraph reworded); both red and green highlights present; character-level diff within modified lines via diff-match-patch charDiff.
high-level-scenarios.S4: side-by-side-mode — toolbar toggle switches to two-pane view; left pane shows baseline (read-only), right pane shows current content (editable); synchronized vertical scroll; pane widths equal.
high-level-scenarios.S6: baseline-from-git — file opened, no .before sibling, file is in git repo with committed version; baseline loaded from `git show HEAD:{path}`; BLOCK_BASELINE_LOADED source=git path=... revision=HEAD.
high-level-scenarios.S7: toggle-cmd-d-enter-exit — in wysiwyg mode, press Cmd+D; diff view appears with baseline fetched async; press Cmd+D again; returns to wysiwyg mode with muya state intact; cursor position preserved. Same flow starting from sourceCode mode restores to sourceCode.
high-level-scenarios.S8: theme-switching-in-diff — railscasts theme active; diff view renders with railscasts CodeMirror theme; switch to one-dark via preferences; diff view re-themes without remount; gutter and highlight colors match theme palette.
high-level-scenarios.S9: tab-switch-preserves-diff-state — tab A in diff mode, tab B in wysiwyg; switch to B then back to A; diff view restored with same baseline and scroll position; no re-fetch of baseline.

failure-scenarios.F1: no-baseline-available — no .before file, not in git repo (or file never committed); Cmd+D shows informative inline banner "No baseline available: file has no .before neighbor and is not tracked by git"; BLOCK_BASELINE_FAILED reason=no_source; diff mode NOT entered; previous mode remains.
failure-scenarios.F2: before-file-outside-sandbox — .before file exists but resolves to path outside SecurityCtx sandbox (e.g., symlink escape); SecurityCtx rejects; BLOCK_BASELINE_FAILED reason=sandbox_violation path=...; error surfaced as inline banner; diff mode NOT entered.
failure-scenarios.F4: empty-file-diff — current file empty, baseline has content (or vice versa, or both empty); MergeView renders correctly (all-green, all-red, or "no differences" message); no crash; BLOCK_DIFF_RENDERED with lines_added/lines_deleted reflecting actual counts including zero.
failure-scenarios.F5: binary-file-opened — file detected as binary (null bytes in first 8KB); diff mode disabled; Cmd+D shows banner "Diff view unavailable for binary files"; BLOCK_DIFF_REJECTED reason=binary_file.
failure-scenarios.F6: large-file-performance-guard — file exceeds 100K lines; diff computation deferred with warning banner "Large file — diff may be slow (N lines). Continue?"; user confirms or cancels; if confirmed, diff computed with progress indicator; BLOCK_LARGE_FILE_WARNING lines=N; if cancelled, BLOCK_DIFF_CANCELLED reason=user_declined_large_file.
failure-scenarios.F7: corrupt-before-file — .before file exists but contains invalid UTF-8; Rust read returns Err; BLOCK_BASELINE_FAILED reason=invalid_utf8 path=...; fallback to git source; if git also fails, F1 path.

race-conditions.R1: edit-during-baseline-fetch — user types in editor while async `mt_diff_baseline` invoke is in-flight; baseline fetch completes, but current content has changed since Cmd+D press; diff view uses CURRENT content at render time (not stale snapshot); small timing window acceptable as diff-match-patch re-diffs on mount; BLOCK_BASELINE_FETCH_ELAPSED_MS logged.
race-conditions.R3: tab-switch-during-baseline-fetch — user presses Cmd+D on tab A, then immediately switches to tab B before baseline returns; invoke response arrives for tab A while tab B is active; response stored in tab A's editor store state; when user switches back to tab A, diff view renders from stored baseline; no orphan render on wrong tab; BLOCK_BASELINE_STORED_DEFERRED tab=A.
race-conditions.R4: rapid-toggle-cmd-d: user double-presses Cmd+D within 100ms; first press initiates baseline fetch, second press should cancel/toggle back; debounce guard: ignore second Cmd+D if baseline fetch in-flight (BLOCK_TOGGLE_DEBOUNCED); OR let second press cancel fetch and return to previous mode (BLOCK_DIFF_CANCELLED reason=rapid_toggle); chosen approach: debounce, 200ms cooldown on Cmd+D.
race-conditions.R5: before-file-deleted-while-diff-open — .before file existed at diff-enter time but is deleted externally while diff view is open; watcher fires; diff view shows stale baseline (acceptable — baseline is a snapshot); banner appears "Baseline file removed — diff shows last loaded baseline"; BLOCK_BASELINE_SOURCE_REMOVED.

numeric-thresholds.T1: Diff render time (MergeView mount + diff-match-patch compute) ≤200ms for 10K-line file on M2 MacBook; BLOCK_DIFF_RENDERED.elapsed_ms measured from baseline-received to first-paint of diff gutter.
numeric-thresholds.T2: Bundle impact: diff-match-patch ≤15KB gzipped; verified by tests/build/bundle-size.test.mjs entry for vendor-diff-match-patch chunk.
numeric-thresholds.T3: MergeView addon: 0 additional network cost (already loaded as part of CodeMirror bundle used by sourceCode.vue); verified by grep of dist/assets/ for merge.js chunk — should be in existing codemirror vendor chunk.
numeric-thresholds.T4: Memory: diff view for 10K-line file ≤50MB additional heap over base editor; measured via `performance.measureUserAgentSpecificMemory()` before/after diff mount; BLOCK_DIFF_MEMORY_DELTA_MB logged in dev mode.
numeric-thresholds.T6: Cmd+D toggle responsiveness: ≤100ms from keypress to diff-view visible (excluding baseline fetch, which shows spinner); ≤50ms from keypress to previous-mode-restored on exit.
numeric-thresholds.T7: Side-by-side scroll sync latency: ≤1 frame (16ms) between panes; visual jank = 0 during synchronized scroll.
numeric-thresholds.T8: Cold-launch impact: 0ms regression on cold-launch first-paint when diff mode NOT active (lazy-loaded); verified against V-M-024/V-M-030 baselines.

edge-cases.E1: no-newline-at-eof — file ends without trailing newline; .before has trailing newline (or vice versa); diff correctly shows the newline difference; MergeView "No newline at end of file" indicator present if applicable.
edge-cases.E2: unicode-content-cjk — file contains CJK characters, emoji (multi-codepoint sequences), RTL (Arabic/Hebrew) text; diff-match-patch handles Unicode correctly (operates on UTF-16 code units); MergeView renders bidirectional text; character-level diff within CJK lines accurate.
edge-cases.E3: very-long-lines — lines exceeding 10K characters; horizontal scroll in both inline and side-by-side modes; no layout overflow or clipping; synchronized horizontal scroll in side-by-side mode.
edge-cases.E4: markdown-with-diff-syntax — file contains fenced code block with ````diff` language tag containing +/- lines; these are NOT interpreted as actual diffs; MergeView diffs the raw markdown source, not rendered output; diff-like content inside code blocks treated as plain text.
edge-cases.E5: before-file-newer-than-current — .before file has mtime newer than current file (unusual but possible if agent wrote .before after user already started editing); diff still computed correctly (baseline = .before content regardless of mtime); BLOCK_BASELINE_MTIME_NEWER logged as info for debugging.
edge-cases.E6: symlinked-before-file — .before is a symlink; resolved path MUST pass SecurityCtx sandbox check (symlink target, not symlink itself); if target outside sandbox, F2 path; if target inside sandbox, normal operation.
edge-cases.E7: identical-files — current content exactly equals baseline; MergeView renders with "No differences" state; all-white gutter (no red/green); BLOCK_DIFF_RENDERED lines_added=0 lines_deleted=0 identical=true.
edge-cases.E8: file-with-windows-line-endings — file uses CRLF, .before uses LF (or mixed); diff-match-patch treats line endings as significant; option to normalize line endings before diff (configurable); default: normalize to LF for diff comparison.
edge-cases.E9: very-large-baseline-from-git — git show returns very large file (>10MB); same 100K-line guard as F6 applied to baseline content; streaming not required (baseline loaded fully into memory for MergeView).
edge-cases.E10: concurrent-before-file-write — external process (Claude agent) writes to .before file while Mark is reading it; Rust fs::read uses single read syscall for small files; for large files, potential partial read; mitigation: retry once on unexpected EOF; BLOCK_BASELINE_READ_RETRY.
edge-cases.E11: diff-mode-with-unsaved-changes — user has unsaved edits in editor; enters diff mode; diff compares baseline against CURRENT BUFFER content (not last-saved disk content); "unsaved changes" indicator still visible; save while in diff mode persists current buffer; diff re-renders if baseline differs from new saved content.
edge-cases.E12: multiple-before-files — both doc.md.before and .before exist in same directory; resolution priority: exact-match `{filename}.before` first; ignore generic `.before`; BLOCK_BASELINE_RESOLUTION strategy=exact_sibling.
edge-cases.E13: readonly-file-diff — file opened as read-only (permissions or preference); diff view left pane read-only (always); right pane also read-only; no edit capability; visual indicator "Read-only" present.
edge-cases.E14: whitespace-only-changes — baseline and current differ only in whitespace (trailing spaces, tab vs spaces, blank lines); diff highlights whitespace changes; option to toggle "ignore whitespace" in diff toolbar; BLOCK_DIFF_RENDERED whitespace_only=true when applicable.

negative-assertions.NA1: diff-match-patch MUST NOT be loaded on cold launch when diff mode is not active — verify vendor-diff-match-patch chunk NOT in initial network waterfall for plain file open; dynamic import() only.
negative-assertions.NA2: MergeView MUST NOT instantiate until baseline is successfully fetched — no empty/null-baseline diff render; BLOCK_DIFF_RENDERED never precedes BLOCK_BASELINE_LOADED in same tab_id trace.
negative-assertions.NA3: .before path MUST NOT bypass SecurityCtx — every mt_diff_baseline call validates resolved path through same sandbox check as mt_read_file; no separate "trusted" path.
negative-assertions.NA4: Diff mode MUST NOT destroy muya instance — entering diff mode hides muya container (display:none or v-show), does NOT unmount; exiting diff mode restores muya visibility; muya selection/cursor state preserved.
negative-assertions.NA5: Diff mode MUST NOT affect file save behavior — Cmd+S in diff mode saves current buffer (right pane content in side-by-side, or current content in inline); baseline (left pane) is NEVER written to disk by save action.
negative-assertions.NA6: git show MUST NOT be invoked with unsanitized path — path argument shell-escaped or passed via stdin/--; no command injection via crafted filenames containing backticks, $(), semicolons, etc.
negative-assertions.NA7: Diff view MUST NOT introduce a Content-Security-Policy violation — diff-match-patch and MergeView operate on string data, no eval(); CSP sha256 hashes unchanged from V-M-024 baseline; no new inline scripts.

LegacyBase.ordering-invariants: (1) BLOCK_DIFF_TOGGLED state=on precedes BLOCK_BASELINE_LOADED|BLOCK_BASELINE_FAILED for same tab_id interaction. (2) BLOCK_BASELINE_LOADED precedes BLOCK_DIFF_RENDERED for same tab_id (no render without baseline). (3) BLOCK_DIFF_TOGGLED state=off precedes next BLOCK_DIFF_TOGGLED state=on for same tab_id (no double-enter). (4) BLOCK_AUTO_DIFF_TRIGGERED precedes BLOCK_BASELINE_LOADED for auto-detected .before files. (5) BLOCK_BASELINE_FAILED with reason=sandbox_violation includes path field matching SecurityCtx rejection log from V-M-010. (6) When diff mode is NOT active for any tab, zero BLOCK_DIFF_REFRESHED markers emitted (no background diffing).

assessment strong
Autonomy trust 0.85/1.0. ~65% deterministic: bundle-size assertions (exact bytes), lazy-load verification (grep dist/), Rust unit tests (.before resolution, sandbox, git show mock), store state assertions, marker ordering invariants. ~25% trace-based: render timing thresholds p95-gated, baseline fetch latency, memory delta measurements. ~10% visual/interactive: diff gutter colors match theme (pixel-diff at 0.1% tolerance for VR snapshots), side-by-side scroll sync (requires frame-level inspection), MergeView layout correctness. Forbidden patterns: setTimeout-based "wait for diff" (use BLOCK_DIFF_RENDERED marker); innerHTML parsing for diff content (use CodeMirror API); headless Chromium for E2E (use tauri-driver WKWebView). Limitation: visual regression baselines for diff color themes require initial human sign-off; git show tests require real git repo initialization in tempdir (deterministic but slow). Agent pipeline end-to-end (Claude writes → Mark shows diff → user edits → Claude reads) requires coordinated multi-process smoke — manual or CI orchestration script.

Debounce: 200ms (DEBOUNCE_TICK). - Project store: project.js:192 _handleWatchEvent receives kind="modify" → calls editorStore.APPLY_FILE_CHANGE('change', { pathname }). - File read: ipcFs.read(path) → invoke('mt::fs::read', { path }) returns UTF-8 string. Scope revision: M-032 is NOT "add watcher + reload from scratch." It is: 1. FIX the broken loadChange path (add ipcFs.read before calling loadChange) 2. PRESERVE cursor/scrollTop across reload (save before Object.assign, restore after) 3. ADD auto-reload for non-dirty files regardless of autoSave preference (new "liveReload" pref, default true) 4. failure-scenarios.F1: file-read-error — external write replaces file with unreadable permissions; ipcFs.read rejects; catch error; show toast "Could not reload: permission denied"; editor keeps old content; BLOCK_RELOAD_FAILED reason=io_error.
failure-scenarios.F3: watcher-stopped — notify-debouncer thread crashes or OS FSEvents limit reached; no events fire; user must manually re-open file; BLOCK_WATCHER_LOST logged when detected via watchdog (future enhancement).
failure-scenarios.F4: tab-closed-during-read — user closes tab while async ipcFs.read is in-flight; read completes; tab no longer in tabs array; loadChange returns early at line 132-143. No crash.

race-conditions.R1: user-types-during-read — user starts typing while async read is pending (100ms settle + read time); isSaved transitions to false during this window; read completes → re-check isSaved: if now false, show conflict notification instead of auto-replacing. GUARD: re-check dirty flag after read.
race-conditions.R2: tab-switch-during-read — user switches tab while read for tab A is pending; read completes; store updates tab A state (not visible); on switch back to A, handleFileChange fires from bus. No wrong-tab contamination.
race-conditions.R3: save-races-reload — user Cmd+S at same instant watcher fires; save writes file (updates mtime), then reload reads file; content from reload matches save content → hash skip → no duplicate work.
race-conditions.R4: two-files-changed-simultaneously — two watcher events for different files; two parallel async reads; each targets correct tab by pathname match. No cross-contamination.

numeric-thresholds.T1: Reload latency (watcher event → editor updated): ≤500ms for files under 100KB on M2 Mac. Breakdown: 200ms debounce + 100ms settle + ~50ms read + ~50ms muya parse. BLOCK_LIVE_RELOAD.elapsed_ms measured from watcher event timestamp.
numeric-thresholds.T2: Debounce: existing 200ms in m013b/watch.rs. Settle delay: 100ms added in APPLY_FILE_CHANGE. Total: 300ms from last write to read attempt.
numeric-thresholds.T3: Memory: reload of 1MB file adds ≤5MB transient heap (two copies of markdown string + muya block tree rebuild). Old blocks GC'd after render.
numeric-thresholds.T4: No main-thread block >50ms: ipcFs.read is async (IPC round-trip); muya.setMarkdown is synchronous but sub-50ms for <100KB files.

edge-cases.E1: Empty file — external tool truncates to 0 bytes; read returns ""; muya.setMarkdown("") → empty editor; no crash.
edge-cases.E2: Same content (touch) — content hash matches; skip reload. Hash: simple string equality (markdown strings are typically <1MB, equality is fast).
edge-cases.E3: Standalone file (no project) — file opened via Cmd+O without project root; no watcher subscription exists; external changes NOT detected. Known limitation. Future: per-tab watcher for standalone files.
edge-cases.E4: Very large file (>1MB) — read + muya.setMarkdown may take >50ms; consider requestIdleCallback for non-active tabs. Active tab: accept the jank for large files.
edge-cases.E5: File renamed externally — watcher fires "remove" + "create"; handled as unlink (banner) + potential re-open if new name matches. Complex edge case; defer to future.

log-markers.M4: [editor][reload][BLOCK_RELOAD_FAILED reason=io_error|parse_error path=... err=...] — read or parse failed

negative-assertions.N1: Reload NEVER silently discards unsaved user edits (isSaved=false MUST trigger conflict flow).
negative-assertions.N2: Reload NEVER fires for same-content writes (hash compare gate).
negative-assertions.N3: loadChange NEVER called with undefined change.data (the latent bug MUST be fixed).
negative-assertions.N4: Reload NEVER runs for files outside open project roots (watcher scope is per-project).

APPLY_FILE_CHANGE calls loadChange({ pathname }) but loadChange expects change.data with file content. FIX: Make APPLY_FILE_CHANGE async. Before loadChange call: await ipcFs.read(pathname) to fetch content, construct data object from content + tab's existing encoding/lineEnding metadata.

loadChange overwrites cursor/scrollTop via Object.assign(tab, newFileState). Cursor and scroll position lost on reload. FIX: Save cursor + scrollTop before Object.assign, restore after. Pass old cursor/scrollTop to bus.emit('file-changed').

edge-cases.E3: manifest-oversized — manifest.yaml exceeds 64KB; rejected before parse with size_exceeded error.
edge-cases.E6: enable-already-enabled — mt_ext_enable called for already-enabled extension; idempotent no-op, secret not rotated; returns current state.
edge-cases.E7: invoke-disabled-extension — mt_ext_invoke called with disabled extension ID; returns MT_EXT_DISABLED error without making HTTP request.
edge-cases.E8: invoke-unknown-extension — mt_ext_invoke called with non-existent extension ID; returns MT_EXT_NOT_FOUND error.
edge-cases.E9: live-server-invalid-auth — POST to /stream/document with wrong or missing Authorization header; server returns 401; document not forwarded; BLOCK_EXT_AUTH_REJECTED reason=invalid_token.
edge-cases.E10: live-server-bind-conflict — configured port already in use; axum server returns bind error; BLOCK_EXT_LIVE_SERVER_BIND status=error reason=address_in_use; app continues without live server (degraded mode).
edge-cases.E11: live-doc-unknown-op (v2) — /stream/patch with op not in {append, replace, replace_section} (e.g. "delete"); apply_section_patch returns SectionPatchError::UnknownOp; handler responds 400; BLOCK_DOC_PATCH_UNKNOWN_OP op=... section=... seq=N.
edge-cases.E12: live-doc-unknown-section (v2) — /stream/patch targeting a section not declared at /stream/open; apply_section_patch returns SectionPatchError::UnknownSection; handler responds 400 (no silent section creation); BLOCK_DOC_PATCH_UNKNOWN_SECTION section=... seq=N.
edge-cases.E13: live-doc-append-to-empty-section (v2) — append op against a section that is empty since open (e.g. summary before first summarizer pass); content becomes the section body; empty sections are skipped by rebuild_document_md so no stray separators appear.

negative-assertions.N1: Extension auth secrets MUST NOT appear in logs — only service name and success/failure status logged; secret value never serialized.
negative-assertions.N2: mt_ext_invoke MUST NOT connect to any address other than 127.0.0.1 — reject manifests with non-loopback host; no DNS resolution.
negative-assertions.N3: Live server MUST NOT bind to 0.0.0.0 — always 127.0.0.1; no external network exposure.
negative-assertions.N4: Extension IPC MUST NOT weaken frontend CSP — all extension communication is backend Rust only (m001_security gate).
negative-assertions.N5: mt_ext_invoke MUST NOT proceed without valid auth secret for the target extension — missing secret = MT_EXT_AUTH_FAILED, not a request without Authorization header.
negative-assertions.N6: /stream/open MUST validate the Bearer token before consulting or disclosing session state — an unauthenticated caller never learns whether a session is active or its session_id (401 precedes 409).

LegacyBase.ordering-invariants: (1) BLOCK_EXT_DISCOVER precedes BLOCK_EXT_ENABLE for any extension ID (cannot enable undiscovered extension). (2) BLOCK_EXT_ENABLE precedes BLOCK_EXT_INVOKE for same extension ID (cannot invoke disabled extension). (3) BLOCK_EXT_AUTH_GENERATED precedes BLOCK_EXT_INVOKE for same extension ID (auth secret must exist before invocation).

LegacyBase.module-surface: Tool: tools/release-preflight.mjs reads package.json, package-lock.json, Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, and src-tauri/tauri.conf.json; validates one exact version and optional v<version> tag. Workflow: .github/workflows/release.yml invokes the metadata preflight before build, runs renderer unit/E2E/typecheck and Rust tests, then requires strict codesign + Gatekeeper evidence before smoke and publication.

high-level-scenarios.S1: All six metadata values across five files contain 2.1.8-beta and tag v2.1.8-beta: preflight passes and emits BLOCK_RELEASE_VERSION_CONSISTENT.
high-level-scenarios.S2: Any metadata source differs: preflight fails with MT_RELEASE_VERSION_MISMATCH and names sources/versions without secrets.
high-level-scenarios.S3: Metadata agrees but tag differs: preflight fails with MT_RELEASE_TAG_MISMATCH before packaging.
high-level-scenarios.S4: Release workflow contains renderer unit/typecheck, a clean-checkout Vite build before bounded Playwright E2E, and Rust test gates before tauri packaging.
high-level-scenarios.S5: Release workflow verifies strict codesign and Gatekeeper acceptance before its installed-app smoke launch and publish job.
high-level-scenarios.S6: Isolated local v2.1.7-beta bundle is ad-hoc re-signed, passes strict codesign, launches separately from the installed Mark instance, and renders a Markdown document without first-input reveal.
high-level-scenarios.S7: The updater feed uses strict SemVer `2.1.7-beta` while release asset URLs retain the canonical Git tag `v2.1.7-beta`.
high-level-scenarios.S8: GitHub publication keeps signed beta tags as normal releases so `/releases/latest/download/latest.json` advances to the newest shipped feed.
high-level-scenarios.S9: Cross-repo cask publication rejects any URL template that does not resolve to the staged `Mark_<version>_aarch64.dmg` release asset.
high-level-scenarios.S10: C-15 MAS variant: `cargo check --no-default-features --features app-store` is a standing gate (V-M-016 command); src-tauri/Entitlements.plist carries app-sandbox + user-selected.read-write + network client/server; mas.conf.json overlay selects the `mas` capability and macOS entitlements and is validated as JSON by CI-side lint; no signing material (certificates, profiles, private keys) is ever committed — .gitignore blocks *.p12/*.p8/*.mobileprovision/*.cer/*.pem/*.key.
